strengths: Teutonic Knights — incredibly durable infantry that excel in sustained combat
Gold-efficient army composition, less reliant on iron mines
Strong defensive positioning with castle-age Halberdiers
Excellent late-game infantry power with unique tech boosts
weaknesses: Villagers move slower — economy builds pace is inherently sluggish
No cavalry bonuses — weak against raiding and map control
Relatively expensive military production compared to eco-focused civs
Limited archer options forces close-range engagements
unique_unit: Teutonic Knight — heavily armored infantry with high HP and armor, excels at holding ground and breaking siege

unique_tech.castle_age: Grunwald — increases attack of soldiers and Halberdiers
unique_tech.imperial_age: Crusade — further attack boost for Teutonic Knights and Halberdiers

economy_bonuses: Gold mines last longer — stretched gold reserves throughout mid-game
Monks heal faster when interacting with Teutonic units
Starting villager moves at normal speed but village production is methodically paced
team_bonus: Gold mines are +20% efficient — valuable for prolonged team games
build_order_notes: Slow but steady economic buildup. Secure gold early to leverage mine efficiency. Transition into Teutonic Knights around Imperial Age with Halberdiers backing. Use defensive castling to buy time for infantry push.
common_pairings: Burgundians — vineyards complement Teuton economy; Burgundian cavalry fills raiding gap
Portuguese — Feitoria boosts late-game economy alongside Teuton gold stretching
Hungarians — Huszars provide raiding coverage that Teutons desperately lack

power_spikes.feudal_age: Weak — slow villager movement hampers aggressive opens
power_spikes.castle_age: Moderate — Halberdiers online but Teutonic Knights still coming
power_spikes.imperial_age: Very strong — fully upgraded Teutonic Knights are nearly unstoppable in sieges
